questions.q: SIP in an index fund vs lump-sum (10-yr evidence):
o: Lump-sum has higher expected return (more time in market); SIP reduces timing regret — behaviour vs math
questions.why: Expected-return math favours more exposure earlier; SIP buys cost-averaging and discipline (behavioural). Answer: no guaranteed winner — state both sides.

questions.q: An open-ended fund NAV: corpus Rs 940 crore, liabilities Rs 40 crore, units 45 crore; NAV per unit is:
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — NAV arithmetic with a liability deduction is a recurring quickie Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Subtract liabilities, then slice by units — never forget the minus.

questions.q: ETFs differ from conventional index funds by:
o: Trading on exchanges intraday with creation/redemption in kind via AMCs
questions.why: ETFs: exchange-listed, intraday price discovery, in-kind creation basket mechanism; index MFs: NAV-based purchase/redemption at day-end.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — structure-vs-pricing distinction Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: The ETF is a fund wearing a stock's badge all day.

questions.q: A fund with 2% TER vs index at 0.2% must outperform gross by at least:
questions.why: Fee drag = differential 1.8% p.a. compounded — active management must beat gross before matching net.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — fee-arithmetic compounding point AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The hurdle isn't the index; it's the index plus your own toll booth.

questions.q: NAV Rs 40; entry load 2% (if any), exit load 1%. The per-unit amounts a new investor pays and receives on exit:
questions.why: Bid = NAV (no repurchase discount beyond exit load): 40×0.99 = 39.60; offer = 40×1.02 = 40.80.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — load-arithmetic is MF chapter's most reliable 1-marker AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Purchase price = NAV × (1+load); sale = NAV × (1−exit load).

questions.q: Scheme assets 900 cr at cost (market 1,000), liabilities 60, units 200 cr. NAV per unit:
questions.why: SEBI valuation norms: investments at market value; NAV = (1,000 − 60)/200 = 4.70 — the trap is valuing at cost (4.20).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — NAV is a market story, not a history story Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: The books remember cost; the unit certificate asks today.

questions.q: Which is NOT part of the recurring total expense ratio of a mutual fund?
questions.why: TER annualises operating expenses (management, trustee, audit, RTA, advertising caps per SEBI); exit load and entry load are transactional — the load is a toll at the gate, the TER is the rent.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — rent inside, toll at the door AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The TER charges your staying; the load charges your leaving.

questions.q: Units of a close-ended scheme are:
o: Traded on the stock exchange, with redemption only on buy-back/liquidation as offered — market price may be below NAV
questions.why: Open-ended = continuous liquidity at NAV; close-ended = a fixed corpus whose units change hands at whatever the exchange says — the discount/premium to NAV is the structural feature to quote in any 2-mark answer.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — NAV sets the open-ended price; the crowd sets the close-ended one AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: An open fund promises a door; a closed fund sells a window seat.
